question_text: Which of the following correctly describes regulatory tox?

options.C: FIFRA does not require efficacy data
options.D: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification

explanation: TSCA regulates chemical substances in commerce through EPA pre-manufacture notification. EPA can require testing and restrict new chemicals

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes regulatory tox?

options.C: FIFRA does not require efficacy data
options.D: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data

explanation: FIFRA requires EPA registration of all pesticides with mammalian toxicity, environmental fate, and efficacy data. Registration must be renewed periodically

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.B: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs

explanation: Subchronic studies are 90-day rodent and 6-month non-rodent studies to identify target organs. Used to establish dose ranges for chronic studies

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.A: Satellite groups always sacrificed at interim
options.B: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential

explanation: Chronic rodent studies are typically 2 years (lifetime) to detect carcinogenic potential. Minimum 50 animals/sex/group for carcinogenicity studies

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.A: Satellite groups always sacrificed at interim
options.B: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies

explanation: Satellite groups provide interim sacrifices or recovery assessments in toxicity studies. Recovery groups assess reversibility of treatment effects

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes study design?

options.B: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%

explanation: The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is the highest dose that does not shorten survival by >10%. Used as high dose in carcinogenicity bioassays

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.B: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality
options.C: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment

explanation: The 2-year rodent bioassay is the gold standard for carcinogenicity assessment. Uses rats and mice at 3 dose levels plus controls

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.A: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays
options.B: Tumor incidence not adjusted for mortality

explanation: The polyk adjustment accounts for differential mortality in carcinogenicity bioassays. Adjusts tumor incidence for animals that died early

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes carcinogenicity?

options.D: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence

explanation: Peto analysis is the preferred statistical method for evaluating tumor incidence. Accounts for competing risks of non-tumor death

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes genetic tox?

options.C: The Ames test uses Salmonella typhimurium strains to detect bacterial reverse mutations

explanation: The Ames test uses Salmonella typhimurium strains to detect bacterial reverse mutations. Strains TA98, TA100 detect different mutation types; S9 provides metabolic activation

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes genetic tox?

options.C: In vivo micronucleus test detects clastogenic and aneugenic effects in bone marrow or blood

explanation: In vivo micronucleus test detects clastogenic and aneugenic effects in bone marrow or blood. OECD TG 474; micronuclei contain chromosome fragments or whole chromosomes

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes genetic tox?

options.C: The comet assay (single-cell gel electrophoresis) detects DNA strand breaks

explanation: The comet assay (single-cell gel electrophoresis) detects DNA strand breaks. Measures tail length and tail moment as indicators of DNA damage

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes genetic tox?

options.A: ICH M3 requires genotoxicity testing battery: Ames, in vitro chromosomal aberration, in vivo micronucleus

explanation: ICH M3 requires genotoxicity testing battery: Ames, in vitro chromosomal aberration, in vivo micronucleus. Must be completed before first human dosing

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes epigenetic?

options.C: DNA methylation at CpG islands typically silences gene expression

explanation: DNA methylation at CpG islands typically silences gene expression. Global hypomethylation and gene-specific hypermethylation are common in cancer

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes epigenetic?

options.C: Histone acetylation is generally associated with active gene transcription

explanation: Histone acetylation is generally associated with active gene transcription. HDACs remove acetyl groups, leading to gene silencing

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.C: ICH S1A requires carcinogenicity studies when drug is used clinically for 6 months or longer
options.D: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: ICH S1A requires carcinogenicity studies when drug is used clinically for 6 months or longer. Also required when carcinogenicity concern exists from SAR or short-term studies

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.D: ICH S1B allows alternative models (transgenic or 6-month) instead of two 2-year bioassays

explanation: ICH S1B allows alternative models (transgenic or 6-month) instead of two 2-year bioassays. Reduces animal use while maintaining detection capability

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.B: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.D: OECD TG 471 describes the bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test)

explanation: OECD TG 471 describes the bacterial reverse mutation test (Ames test). Uses Salmonella and/or E. coli with and without metabolic activation

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.D: OECD TG 474 describes the mammalian erythrocyte micronucleus test

explanation: OECD TG 474 describes the mammalian erythrocyte micronucleus test. Bone marrow or peripheral blood in mice or rats

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: GLP not required for safety studies
options.B: GLP regulations require nonclinical studies to be conducted per predetermined protocols with QA oversight
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: GLP regulations require nonclinical studies to be conducted per predetermined protocols with QA oversight. Key elements: QA unit, SOPs, study director, raw data archival

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.B: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.C: OECD GLP requires a Quality Assurance Program separate from the study director
options.D: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: OECD GLP requires a Quality Assurance Program separate from the study director. QA performs inspections and audits to ensure data integrity

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.B: ICH Q3A requires identification of impurities above the identification threshold in drug substances
options.D: GLP not required for safety studies

explanation: ICH Q3A requires identification of impurities above the identification threshold in drug substances. Threshold depends on maximum daily dose

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.B: GLP not required for safety studies
options.C: S1A requires studies for all drugs
options.D: ICH S7B requires hERG channel assay and telemetry study for QT prolongation assessment

explanation: ICH S7B requires hERG channel assay and telemetry study for QT prolongation assessment. In vitro hERG + in vivo conscious animal telemetry

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes guidelines?

options.A: ICH S10 requires photosafety evaluation when drug has significant skin absorption
options.C: GLP not required for safety studies
options.D: S1A requires studies for all drugs

explanation: ICH S10 requires photosafety evaluation when drug has significant skin absorption. Includes in vitro phototoxicity and in vivo photosafety assessment

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes epa regulations?

options.A: EPA does not require risk assessment
options.B: EPA GLP (40 CFR 160) applies to FIFRA testing; 40 CFR 792 applies to TSCA testing

explanation: EPA GLP (40 CFR 160) applies to FIFRA testing; 40 CFR 792 applies to TSCA testing. Similar to 21 CFR 58 but specific to EPA-regulated testing

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes epa regulations?

options.B: The Red Book describes EPA's four-step risk assessment paradigm
options.D: EPA does not require risk assessment

explanation: The Red Book describes EPA's four-step risk assessment paradigm. Hazard ID, dose-response, exposure assessment, risk characterization

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes dose response?

options.A: NOAEL is the highest dose with no statistically significant adverse effect increase

explanation: NOAEL is the highest dose with no statistically significant adverse effect increase. LOAEL is the lowest dose with significant effect

question_text: Which of the following correctly describes dose response?

options.B: Benchmark dose (BMD) uses the full dose-response dataset rather than relying on a single NOAEL

explanation: Benchmark dose (BMD) uses the full dose-response dataset rather than relying on a single NOAEL. BMD10 = dose for 10% response above background

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding dose response EXCEPT:

options.A: Uncertainty factors (UFs) are applied to NOAEL or BMD to derive RfDs or RfCs

explanation: Uncertainty factors (UFs) are applied to NOAEL or BMD to derive RfDs or RfCs. Standard UFs: 10x interspecies, 10x intraspecies, 3-10x LOAEL-to-NOAEL

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding species selection EXCEPT:

options.B: Only one species needed for all studies
options.D: The rat is the most commonly used species in acute toxicity studies

explanation: The rat is the most commonly used species in acute toxicity studies. Mice, rabbits, and guinea pigs also used per regulatory requirements

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding species selection EXCEPT:

options.B: Non-rodent species (dogs, NHPs) are required in subchronic studies for drugs intended for chronic use
options.D: Only one species needed for all studies

explanation: Non-rodent species (dogs, NHPs) are required in subchronic studies for drugs intended for chronic use. Provides assessment in a second species

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding statistical EXCEPT:

options.B: Pairwise always more powerful than trend
options.C: Cochran-Armitage trend test assesses dose-related trends in tumor incidence

explanation: Cochran-Armitage trend test assesses dose-related trends in tumor incidence. More powerful than pairwise comparisons when dose-response exists

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding statistical EXCEPT:

options.A: Pairwise always more powerful than trend
options.C: Historical control data account for spontaneous tumor rates varying by strain, sex, and facility

explanation: Historical control data account for spontaneous tumor rates varying by strain, sex, and facility. Essential for interpreting tumor findings in bioassays

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding quality assurance EXCEPT:

options.A: Study director also serves as QA
options.B: QA unit must be independent of the study director with access to all study records
options.D: Raw data can be destroyed after study

explanation: QA unit must be independent of the study director with access to all study records. Inspects studies at intervals and reports to management

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding quality assurance EXCEPT:

options.A: Raw data can be destroyed after study
options.C: Study director also serves as QA
options.D: Raw data must be archived for minimum 10 years for FDA-regulated studies

explanation: Raw data must be archived for minimum 10 years for FDA-regulated studies. Includes all original observations, records, and photographs

question_text: All of the following are correct regarding quality assurance EXCEPT:

options.A: Raw data can be destroyed after study
options.C: Study director also serves as QA
options.D: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are required for all GLP-compliant studies

explanation: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) are required for all GLP-compliant studies. SOPs ensure consistency and reproducibility of methods

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes membrane transport?

options.A: Small hydrophilic molecules (up to about 600 Da) permeate membranes through aqueous pores via paracellular diffusion

explanation: Small hydrophilic molecules (up to about 600 Da) permeate membranes through aqueous pores via paracellular diffusion. Fick's law governs simple diffusion - chemicals move from higher to lower concentration without energy expenditure

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes membrane transport?

options.B: Lipid solubility is determined by the octanol/water partition coefficient (log P), with positive values indicating high lipid solubility

explanation: Lipid solubility is determined by the octanol/water partition coefficient (log P), with positive values indicating high lipid solubility. DDT has log P of 6.76, TCDD has log P of 7.05

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes membrane transport?

options.A: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation describes pH as a function of pKa for weak organic acids and bases

explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation describes pH as a function of pKa for weak organic acids and bases. For acids: pH - pKa = log([ionized]/[nonionized]); for bases: pKa - pH = log([nonionized]/[ionized])

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes membrane transport?

options.A: Active transport requires energy, exhibits saturability, selectivity, and competitive inhibition

explanation: Active transport requires energy, exhibits saturability, selectivity, and competitive inhibition. Metabolic poisons block active transport by inhibiting ATP production

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes membrane transport?

options.C: Facilitated transport does not require energy input and is not affected by metabolic poisons

explanation: Facilitated transport does not require energy input and is not affected by metabolic poisons. Glucose transport from GI tract occurs via facilitated diffusion

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes transporters?

options.C: P-glycoprotein (MDR1/ABCB1) was the first active xenobiotic transporter identified, functioning as an efflux pump

explanation: P-glycoprotein (MDR1/ABCB1) was the first active xenobiotic transporter identified, functioning as an efflux pump. ABC transporter superfamily has 7 subfamilies with 49 genes in humans

question_text: Which quantitative relationship correctly describes transporters?

options.C: MRP2 and MRP3 efflux xenobiotic metabolites conjugated with glucuronic acid or glutathione

explanation: MRP2 and MRP3 efflux xenobiotic metabolites conjugated with glucuronic acid or glutathione. Acetaminophen glucuronide is a substrate for both MRP2 and MRP3

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating transporters should consider which of the following?

options.B: BCRP (ABCG2) functions as homodimers linked by disulfide bridges at cysteine 603, with MW ~70 kDa

explanation: BCRP (ABCG2) functions as homodimers linked by disulfide bridges at cysteine 603, with MW ~70 kDa. MDR1 is ~170 kDa, MRP1 is ~190 kDa

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating transporters should consider which of the following?

options.B: OATP1B1 polymorphisms decrease hepatic extraction, increasing systemic exposure to substrates like statins

explanation: OATP1B1 polymorphisms decrease hepatic extraction, increasing systemic exposure to substrates like statins. Decreased OATP1B1 function increases myopathy risk

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating transporters should consider which of the following?

options.B: OCT2 mediates cisplatin uptake into kidney, contributing to dose-limiting nephrotoxicity

explanation: OCT2 mediates cisplatin uptake into kidney, contributing to dose-limiting nephrotoxicity. OCT1 mediates metformin uptake into liver

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating absorption should consider which of the following?

options.B: The three main barriers for toxicant absorption are the GI tract, lungs, and skin
options.D: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics

explanation: The three main barriers for toxicant absorption are the GI tract, lungs, and skin. Only caustic/corrosive chemicals act directly at point of contact

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating absorption should consider which of the following?

options.A: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics
options.D: Weak organic acids are absorbed more readily from the stomach (pH ~2) where they are nonionized

explanation: Weak organic acids are absorbed more readily from the stomach (pH ~2) where they are nonionized. Organic bases are absorbed predominantly in the intestine

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating absorption should consider which of the following?

options.B: Requires active transport for all xenobiotics
options.D: First-pass effect (presystemic elimination) removes chemicals before systemic circulation entry

explanation: First-pass effect (presystemic elimination) removes chemicals before systemic circulation entry. High first-pass effect limits toxic potential

question_text: A toxicologist evaluating absorption should consider which of the following?

options.A: The small intestine increases surface area approximately 600-fold through villi and microvilli

explanation: The small intestine increases surface area approximately 600-fold through villi and microvilli. This overcomes low nonionized fraction at intestinal pH
